newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crop progress highlights - USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crop progress highlights - USDA.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Monday said 46 percent of the U.S. soybean crop was planted versus 20 percent last week, and 14 percent in the same period a year ago.
The five-year average for soybean plantings was 26 percent.
In its report on conditions for the week ended May 18, USDA said 88 percent of the corn crop was planted versus 61 percent a year ago and the five-year average of 67 percent.
USDA said five percent of the U.S. winter wheat crop was in very poor condition, 12 percent in poor, 33 percent fair, 40 percent good and 10 percent excellent.
Fifty-nine percent of the spring wheat crop was planted compared with 45 percent a year ago and the five-year average of 70 percent.
USDA also said 24 percent of the spring wheat crop was emerged compared with 19 percent in the same period last year and the five-year average of 44 percent.

The department reported 65 percent of the cotton crop was planted, compared with 65 percent in the same period in 1996 and the five-year average of 65 percent. -- Washington Commodities Desk (202) 898-8394
